caption: The drawing is an overhead view of a landscaped estate labeled "The John B. Bull Estate — The Blackwell Survey 1860." It shows two large rectangular buildings with red-pink roofs, one at the lower center and another at the upper left. Both buildings are surrounded by decorative, curvilinear gardens with yellow, green, and blue-green borders and geometric designs. Adjacent to the upper-left building are evenly spaced plots, possibly gardens or fields, and to its left, a border of circular, blue-green trees runs vertically. In the upper half of the estate, there are four square parterre-style garden sections containing swirling, pastel pink, white, and green patterns with a circular lawn in the center. The bottom half features similar geometric garden beds around the main building. Surrounding the estate are boulevards lined with more blue-green and yellow-green trees, with large open grassy areas, some in deep olive green and others in lighter yellow-green shades. Paths and roads outlined in off-white or tan border all areas, delineating the different zones within the estate.
title: John B. Bull Garden
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
